ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-11-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Brought to the emergency department by friends because of erratic behavior with paranoid ideation and grandiose delusions.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the emergency department ten months after a previous encounter for erratic behavior and substance use. They report that he has been increasingly anxious, irritable, and has been talking non-stop about starting a business that will "change the world." He has also been suspicious of his neighbors, claiming they are spying on him. The patient admits to using a substance but is vague about the details.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Cocaine intoxication (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Open reduction internal fixation of left wrist fracture (age 16)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Alcohol use disorder
- Paternal uncle: Bipolar disorder
- Mother: Hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Mention he has been attending frequent parties and staying out late.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows: BP 160/100 mmHg, HR 120 bpm, Temp 99.8°F (37.7°C), RR 22/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the patient is agitated, sweating profusely, and has dilated pupils.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urine toxicology screen is positive for cocaine.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Brought to the emergency department by friends because of erratic behavior that started 2 hours ago after attending a party.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
His friends report that he was at a party where he seemed to be his usual self until he suddenly became very talkative, agitated, and started making grandiose plans about starting a new business venture.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Open reduction internal fixation of left wrist fracture (age 16)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Alcohol use disorder
- Paternal uncle: Bipolar disorder
- Mother: Hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Current social smoker (approximately 5 cigarettes/weekend). Alcohol: Heavy episodic/binge drinking (6-8 drinks per occasion, 3-4 nights per week). Occupation: Account executive.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows: temperature 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure 160/100 mmHg, pulse 120/min, and respiratory rate 22/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the patient is restless, has dilated pupils, and is sweating profusely. His speech is rapid and he appears to be responding to internal stimuli.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urine toxicology screen is positive for cocaine.
